question: A woman who delivered vaginally 36 hours ago and had no postpartum complications requests an IUCD. Which of the following statements about PPIUCD insertion is CORRECT?

answers.text: She is no longer eligible; PPIUCD must be inserted within 10 minutes of placenta delivery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: PPIUCD insertion within 10 minutes of placenta delivery is 'immediate postpartum' — but the window extends to 48 hours postpartum (called 'early PPIUCD'). At 36 hours, she is still within the window.

answers.text: She is eligible; PPIUCD can be inserted within 48 hours of delivery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The PPIUCD insertion window is 48 hours postpartum. At 36 hours after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery, she meets the eligibility criteria. After 48 hours, there is an interval of exclusion until 4 weeks postpartum due to uterine involution risk.

answers.text: She should receive an emergency contraceptive pill (ECP) instead, as IUCD is contraindicated in the postpartum period

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: IUCD is not contraindicated postpartum — PPIUCD is specifically designed for this window. ECP is used for unprotected intercourse, not routine postpartum family planning.

answers.text: She can have the IUCD inserted at any time up to 6 weeks postpartum

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The 6-week timeframe is incorrect. After 48 hours, there is an exclusion interval until 4 weeks postpartum (involution risk). Interval IUCD insertion resumes after 4–6 weeks, but this is not a continuous window.

overallFeedback.feedback: PPIUCD can be inserted within 48 hours of delivery. At 36 hours, this woman is still within the window. After 48 hours, insertion is deferred until at least 4 weeks postpartum.
Well done! The PPIUCD window is 48 hours postpartum — a critical clinical threshold. After 48 h until 4 weeks, insertion is generally avoided.
